Name: Mike Jones
Question: I would like to go through the trans process. Is there any way you can put me through or help with a doctor contact?
Answer: Hello, Madeee. I’d really like to be able to help you, but as at least one other answer pointed out I don’t know anything about you including where you live. You have been the victim of extremely poor user experience (UX) design by Quora; it’s a problem that’s been around for years and they seem to have no interest in fixing it. So since I can’t help you with your question as asked, let me see if I can help you with asking it in a way that’s more likely to actually get you help: When I look at your profile page, I see that you joined Quora this month (March 2024) and your only Quora activity is this question. When I look a little deeper by clicking on the “Activity” link on your profile I find this: That’s also the one Quora user you’re currently following. From that, I conclude that what you wanted to do was send your question specifically to Mia Rosenbloom. Unfortunately, what you actually did was send it out to the Quora community generally where it will show up in some fraction of 3–400 million Quora feeds. It’s an understandable mistake, because Quora somewhat inexplicably puts an “Ask” button on each Quora profile page which often creates the quite reasonable thought that if you click on that link on another person’s profile page, you’re sending a question directly to them. Unfortunately, that’s not what happens. They will see the question in their feed (I believe — I haven’t tested this) but it will also be shown to a lot of other people. To accomplish what it looks like you intended to do, you should have sent a private message to Mia. Quora doesn’t make this simple. To do it, you have to go to your profile, select “Messages”, then create the message and select the recipient. Further, they have to have their account set up to accept messages. It is, to put it mildly, a terrible design and results in users (especially newer users) doing this on a regular basis. I hope you get the answer you’re looking for, and I hope this may help you get that more directly the next time you’re in this situation.

Name: Mike Jones
Question: Why is fielding so lousy in Major League Baseball today (and please don't point to fielding statistics. Rarely are errors called today, so fielding percentages are not an accurate reflection of fielding in the modern game)?
Answer: Before asking why, ask if. I’ve long said that fielding percentages are more noise than signal, so I’m certainly not going to use them. But how about using the % of batted balls in play that are turned into outs? Let’s start with PA. That includes every batting event. Then we’ll remove BB, HBP, K, and HR as events that the defense has no chance to field. I went back and forth about taking out sac bunts, but a) they do need to get fielded and b) there aren’t that many of them. We’ll also take out GIDP because that’s the defense getting two outs on one successfully fielded ball. That’s our denominator, the number of balls in play the defense has a chance to field. Let’s call it “BIP”. For the numerator, we want the number of outs on balls in play. That’s AB-H-K. So the net is (AB-H-K-GIDP) / (PA-BB-K-HR). Let’s actually take 1 minus that so it looks like a batting average. What does that look like over time? Well, it’s easy to get that data at league level from baseball-reference.com for the AL or NL. I’ll take <flips coin> the NL. So what do we see? Note that this entire graph is between .250 and .350, so the range may appear magnified. So does it look like fielding is bad now? Well…maybe. If we’re going to take this at face value, then something happened around 1992 to make it sharply worse, and that it’s been on a slight trend of getting better since 2014. I’m skeptical that the entire NL basically went clumsy around 1992, so I spent a few minutes looking for something that might better explain that, but I didn’t find anything. I looked at 2B/BIP and HR/BIP thinking that those might indicate a higher percentage of harder-hit balls that would be harder to field, but it didn’t correlate well at all. Neither did HR/PA and K/PA. The one other interesting thing about the graph is it looks like the season-to-season variance is pretty steadily decreasing. Until 1944, we see some pretty big swings. From 1944–1992, smaller swings, and since then even smaller ones. I’m open to any suggestions of things to look at to explain that 1992 jump, though.

Question: If a team is out of mound visits, but their reliever has not faced the minimum number of batters, and the catcher walks to the mound, what happens?
Answer: Rule 5.11(m)(4) If a position player makes a visit after his team has exhausted its allotted number of mound visits he may be subject to ejection for failing to return to his position when instructed by the umpire; however, an impermissible visit by a position player shall not require the removal of the pitcher.
